correctness.rationale: The polynomial Artin–Schreier cover has a unique pole of order \(M=1+(p-1)d\) prime to \(p\), hence genus \((p-1)^2d/2\). Its scalar group has exactly two totally ramified tame quotient points and yields genus \((p-1)d/2\). The invariant one-pole functions \(u\) and \(uv^j\) have orders \(p\) and \(p+j(d-1)\). The explicit Apéry set produces the exact genus, proving equality of semigroups by the gap theorem. Minimality, conductor and pseudo-Frobenius set are deduced from residue-class arguments. The proof covers every allowed \(p,d\) and all coefficients of f; the finite checker is supplementary.

originality.rationale: The inspected May 2026 linearized-function-field paper assumes a separable constant-coefficient additive polynomial over a rational base and a Galois cover. Here the natural degree-p projection has tame index p-1 above u=0, hence cannot be Galois. The contemporaneous Kummer-extension theorem treats Galois cyclic degree-prime-to-characteristic covers. Searches for the exact variable-coefficient equation and generator formula did not locate equivalent full claims. Residual historical-coverage risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An older theorem about the semigroup of a tame quotient of an Artin–Schreier curve may be indexed under invariant-theoretic language not found by targeted searches.
Alternative rational functions could express some special members as Galois covers of another base; the non-Galois statement is only for the natural u-projection.
The abstract-only Kummer reference and other uninspected manuscripts do not exclude a historically prior implicit specialization.

value.rationale: The all-polynomial, non-Galois family has a full coefficient-invariant one-point semigroup of maximal embedding dimension, complete minimal generators, conductor and numerical type. These structural invariants are motivated by the contemporary focus on ramified-point gaps and their use in the Riemann–Roch theory of curves and algebraic-geometric codes; the result is not a fixed small example or a trivial renaming of a known Galois formula.
